findings.title: Global canManage() grants manage on view-only permission
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). Anyone with only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource therefore passes canManage(), which gates group creation, update, delete and child creation. Per-group canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires only MANAGE, so global and per-object checks disagree and view-only admins gain write access.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource ID instead of group ID
findings.body: The method iterates resources of type Groups whose names are group IDs, but calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the result. Resource.getId() is the internal authz UUID, not the group ID stored in the resource name. The lookup by name then misses, falls back to the all-groups resource, and the returned set contains authz IDs that callers use as group IDs for user search/count filtering, so filtering is wrong and no users or wrong users are returned.

findings.title: NPE when all-groups type resource does not exist
findings.body: hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) which can return null if the type resource was never created or was deleted, then unconditionally calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). That dereferences a null resource and turns a permission check into a 500 error.

findings.title: NPE when all-users type resource does not exist
findings.body: UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission() loads the all-users type resource as fallback and calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. If the Users type resource is missing, any per-user view/manage/map-roles/membership check throws NullPointerException instead of denying.

findings.title: getScope() NPEs on unknown resource type
findings.body: getScope() does SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking that resourceType exists. An unknown or null resource type causes NullPointerException instead of the intended ModelValidationException about scope not found for resource type.

findings.title: getResourceName() only resolves Users, not Groups
findings.body: getResourceName() special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE to return 'All users' or the username, but has no branch for GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE or CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE. Group permission resources therefore fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not set for schema-created resources, yielding null/wrong display names in admin UI/API responses.
